newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman limits ownership of local bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Oman limits ownership of local bank shares.

text.p: Oman's Central Bank, in a move to widen the shareholder base of local banks, limited individual and company share ownership in any one of the seven local banks to between 15 and 35 percent, a statement said.

"The aggregate holding by an individual and his related parties shall not exceed 15 percent of the voting shares in a locally incorporated bank," the central bank statement received by Reuters on Sunday said.
It said the holding of an incorporated body and its related parties and that of a joint stock company or holding company should not exceed 25 and 35 percent respectively.
"The move comes within the framework of (efforts to) re-organise share ownership in local banks," said Central Bank Executive President Hamoud bin Sanjour Hashem.
He said the ceiling, introduced for the first time in Oman, would minimise the concentration of shares in individual or company portfolios, which he said could affect performance.
It was not clear whether current shareholders would have to liquidate existing portfolios to meet the new requirements.
The statement also said that investors holding 10 percent or more of any local bank's shares could not subscribe to more than 15 percent of shares on offer by another local bank.
Sanjour said local banks had been notified of the new regulations that would take effect one month after publication in the official gazette. No publication date was given.
Analysts said the new measures by Oman, a small independent oil-producing Gulf state, were in line with its policy to channel savings into the local economy.
The new measures do not apply to 11 foreign banks and three specialised government banks working in Oman.
